meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Then take it out, Hale, and tell me what you actually have besides a score.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
I'm writing down the date, Hale. Show me the note itself, the page with the date on it. A seventeen-year-old put on the spot and answering "like, being stuck" doesn't tell me who wrote the essay.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

I'm writing that down, Hale: October 15 outline, essay with no mention of cowardice. Students change their argument between an outline and a draft, and teachers usually call that revising. Put both pages in front of me and I'll read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's procedure 4.4, Hale, so you're offering me what your own policy already requires. Is it private, with no other students in the room, and does the zero stay on his gradebook until then? I still haven't seen the outline or the note, and I'm not agreeing to anything until I do.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that entering the zero before calling me was your mistake, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record, to be sent to me in writing. I still demand the zero withdrawn, the November 2 note and the October 15 outline shown to me, the rewrite held privately, and a written promise that nothing goes on his file. I expect your written offer by Friday at 3 PM.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, still demanding the zero withdrawn; she did not accept the supervised rewrite and wanted the documents and privacy terms first.
What moved her: the October 15 outline arguing cowardice against an essay that never mentions it.
